title: Convert persistent EC2 and RDS workloads from on-demand into committed-use coverage
recommended_action: Convert persistent EC2 and RDS workloads from on-demand into committed-use coverage
buyer_ask: Move persistent workloads into committed-use coverage.
negotiation_language: Ask AWS to convert stable EC2 and RDS run rate into commitment coverage only after owner validation confirms the workloads are durable.
vendor_concession: AWS gives up pure on-demand pricing on durable run-rate demand.
timing_dependency: Before the next EDP commitment review.
risk_if_ignored: Persistent workloads keep paying on-demand premiums.
native_vs_nexus_note: AWS Cost Explorer shows coverage; Nexus links it to EDP terms, apps, AP spend, and renewal action.

title: Downsize low-utilization production compute after owner validation
recommended_action: Downsize low-utilization production compute after owner validation
buyer_ask: Downsize low-utilization production compute after owner sign-off.
negotiation_language: Ask workload owners to approve right-sizing for consistently underused resources, then sequence changes through normal change windows.
vendor_concession: AWS gives up unnecessary oversized consumption on validated workloads.
timing_dependency: Before the next monthly optimization review.
risk_if_ignored: Low-utilization spend remains embedded in the run-rate baseline.
native_vs_nexus_note: Compute Optimizer may recommend shape changes; Nexus checks owner, app criticality, and contract timing before action.

title: Reduce avoidable cross-region and internet data-transfer charges on patient digital workloads
recommended_action: Reduce avoidable cross-region and internet data-transfer charges on patient digital workloads
buyer_ask: Reduce avoidable cross-region and internet transfer charges.
negotiation_language: Ask architecture and application owners to redesign avoidable data-transfer paths before treating the spend as unavoidable baseline.
vendor_concession: AWS consumption shifts away from avoidable transfer patterns where architecture changes are approved.
timing_dependency: Before the next architecture review board.
risk_if_ignored: Network charges continue to grow without accountable workload ownership.
native_vs_nexus_note: Native tools show the spend. Nexus asks which application owns it and whether architecture or contract action is the right mitigation.

title: Review enterprise support tier charges against actual support usage and escalation profile
recommended_action: Review enterprise support tier charges against actual support usage and escalation profile
buyer_ask: Review enterprise support charges against actual support demand.
negotiation_language: Ask AWS to reprice or credit support economics where escalation demand does not justify the current support tier.
vendor_concession: AWS gives up support-tier economics not backed by observed support demand.
risk_if_ignored: Support charges stay disconnected from actual service demand.
native_vs_nexus_note: Nexus converts support spend into a commercial review, not an engineering-only dashboard note.

title: Reserve steady Azure VM and SQL capacity for analytics workloads
recommended_action: Reserve steady Azure VM and SQL capacity for analytics workloads
buyer_ask: Reserve steady Azure VM and SQL capacity.
negotiation_language: Ask Microsoft to align reservation coverage to stable analytics workloads after confirming the workload owners and expected duration.
vendor_concession: Microsoft gives up on-demand economics on durable VM and SQL demand.
timing_dependency: Before the next EA commitment review.
risk_if_ignored: Durable workloads continue paying avoidable on-demand rates.
native_vs_nexus_note: Azure Advisor shows candidates. Nexus ties them to the EA commitment, data-platform owner, and finance action state.

title: Schedule non-production analytics pools and retire idle storage attached to old reporting jobs
recommended_action: Schedule non-production analytics pools and retire idle storage attached to old reporting jobs
buyer_ask: Schedule or retire non-production analytics pools.
negotiation_language: Ask workload owners to approve scheduling and retention decisions before any idle Synapse spend is counted as removable.
vendor_concession: Microsoft consumption decreases where non-production analytics pools can be safely scheduled or retired.
risk_if_ignored: Idle analytics spend remains in the baseline without retention evidence.
native_vs_nexus_note: Nexus requires workload owner and data-retention review before labeling it removable spend.

title: Close owner and application tag gaps before making business-unit savings claims
recommended_action: Close owner and application tag gaps before making business-unit savings claims
buyer_ask: Close tag gaps before claiming business-unit savings.
negotiation_language: Ask application and platform owners to remediate owner and application tags before assigning savings to a business unit.
vendor_concession: No vendor concession; this is a buyer control action before value attribution.
timing_dependency: Before savings attribution or finance handoff.
risk_if_ignored: Savings claims may be misallocated or unsupported.
native_vs_nexus_note: This is intentionally a blocker, not a savings claim.

title: Keep billing export and AP-paid invoice reconciliation matched before any savings claim
recommended_action: Keep billing export and AP-paid invoice reconciliation matched before any savings claim
buyer_ask: Keep billing exports reconciled to AP-paid invoices.
negotiation_language: Ask Finance and Cloud FinOps to maintain billing-to-AP reconciliation before any cloud optimization is treated as paid-spend value.
vendor_concession: No vendor concession; this is a finance control requirement.
risk_if_ignored: Cloud billing exports may be mistaken for finance-confirmed spend.
native_vs_nexus_note: Nexus does not treat cloud billing exports as paid spend until AP confirms the invoice.
